issues: Integrity is fine: the diff only changes Block.forward to put an RMSNorm on the attention and MLP branch outputs before they are added to the residual stream. It does not touch the val_bpb measurement, data loading, seed lines, the prepare.py import or the evaluation call.

No bug makes the result meaningless. This is a legitimate architecture change. One modelling caveat: norm() has no learnable gain, so each block now adds a fixed unit-RMS update and cannot learn how much each branch contributes. Also, if c_proj is zero-initialised, the norm of a near-zero branch output gives very large gradients early in training. Either could explain the worse score, but neither is an integrity problem.

The numbers agree with the decision. The candidate scored 1.1385 against an incumbent mean of 1.1145 over 16 runs, so it is 0.024 worse (higher bpb). A z of -4.249 under the convention (incumbent − candidate)/sd points the right way and supports reject. There are no claims in the submission that conflict with these numbers.

z cannot be recomputed because the incumbent's standard deviation is not given. Back-solving from the reported z, the sd implied is about 0.0056 if z = diff/sd, or about 0.0055 if z = diff/(sd·sqrt(1+1/16)). Either seems plausible for run-to-run noise.
There is only one candidate run, but at z ≈ -4.2 a replicate would almost certainly not change the reject, so it is not worth spending a slot.
